sd_new_domentions.blurb: A cluster of small granite domes in the Needles of Rushmore country near Keystone, South Dakota, reached from the Iron Mountain side. The 13 climbs here are mainly traditional lines with a couple of bolted ones, and the grades run from 5.7 up through a good block of 5.10s, with a pair of 5.11s at the top. Routes tend to be around 100 feet, and the rock varies by face from very solid to merely good. Expect long rappels, so bring a long rope. The domes see little traffic, which suits climbers who want a quiet day on short, moderate granite.

tx_sex_canyon.blurb: A long, steep limestone wall at Reimers Ranch outside Austin, further down the canyon from Sex Cave. All 17 routes are bolted, and the grades are for strong climbers: mostly 5.12 with several 5.13s and a single 5.10. The wall overhangs, with stalactites low down in places, and stays shaded for most of the day. It also stays largely dry in a light shower, except up high on the routes. When the neighbouring cave is crowded, this wall is the usual fallback. Holds can stay wet for days after heavy rain, so give it time to dry.

tx_warm_up_roof.blurb: A roofed boulder on East Mountain at Hueco Tanks, east of El Paso, and a popular first stop for loosening up before the harder boulders nearby. The wall is steep, around 60 degrees, with jugs to pull on. Its 17 problems cover a wide range: a handful of easy ones, a solid middle of V4 to V5, and a few hard problems at the top end, including some very hard recent additions. Kids Stuff sits back to back on the other side of the boulder, with a short vertical wall and a small low roof holding mostly easier problems.
